title: Traefik default rule-length priority, stripPrefix, Host matcher
claims: with default priorities the longer rule (PathPrefix /a/b) wins for /a/b/c
Host() restricts routing; another Host is not forwarded
not_claimed: PathPrefix string-prefix matching of /a against /ab (not probed)
source_semantics: Traefik router priority defaults to the rule string length, so the longer, more specific rule wins here; stripPrefix removes the matching prefix before forwarding; no matching router yields 404. Documentation-inferred unless the upstream differential runs. The static configuration is the harness's own (upstream.example.json): one plaintext loopback entryPoint `web` with no TLS, middlewares, redirections or forwarded-header settings, and no router names entryPoints, so the case passes the converter's operator assertion traefik-entrypoints-add-no-controls (without it every forwarding router is refused).
